anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch) the SPI control nets are attached to ESP32-C3 GPIOs one position lower than the firmware expects: the CS0 label sits on the pin row named GPIO03/ADC1_CH3 (U1 pin 6), SCK on GPIO04/ADC1_CH4 (pin 19), CS1 on GPIO05/ADC2_CH0 (pin 20), CS2 on GPIO06 (pin 21); only SO on GPIO10 (pin 16) is correct. (GPIO07/pin 22 is left unconnected.)
anomalies.expected: The specification and firmware require SCK=GPIO5, SO=GPIO10, CS0=GPIO4, CS1=GPIO6, CS2=GPIO7 (shared SPI bus with three independent chip-selects).

evidence.quote: SCK (pin 5) and SO (pin 7, tri-state/MISO) are common nets (SCK, SO) tied to all three ICs and to the ESP32 (U1 GPIO5/SCK, GPIO10/SO). Each chip has its own independent chip-select: ~{CS} (pin 6) on U2/U3/U4 goes to separate nets CS0/CS1/CS2, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively.
SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7
mcu.kicad_sch, right edge of U1: CS0 box on row 'GPIO03/ADC1_CH3', SCK on 'GPIO04/ADC1_CH4', CS1 on 'GPIO05/ADC2_CH0', CS2 on 'GPIO06', SO on 'GPIO10'.

anomalies.impact: The firmware would toggle/clock the wrong pins: its SCK (GPIO5) is wired to the CS1 line, its CS0 (GPIO4) to the SCK line, etc. The MAX31855 thermocouple SPI reads would fail or select the wrong zone, so temperature sensing would not work as intended.

anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet a second screw terminal J5 (Screw_Terminal_01x02) is wired between the HEATER net (the 3.3 V logic control line from ESP32 GPIO1 / U6 IN+DIAG_EN) and GND, in addition to the heater load connector J6 on U6 OUT.
anomalies.expected: The intended heater path has only one screw terminal, J6, on the switched 12 V OUT of U6; there is no user connector on the 3.3 V heater-control net.

evidence.quote: OUT (pin 7) feeds the heater connector J6 pin 2 ... A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net
mcu.kicad_sch: J5 pin 2 tied to the HEATER vertical wire (same node as D2 anode and U6 IN/DIAG_EN), J5 pin 1 tied to GND.

anomalies.impact: The J5 terminal serves no function in the reference design; inserting a plug or jumper across it would short the heater drive signal to ground, preventing the high-side switch from turning the heater on.

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the intended design: the SPI clock and the three thermocouple chip-selects are connected to ESP32 GPIOs shifted one position low (GPIO3/4/5/6 instead of the firmware's GPIO4/5/6/7), and an extra screw terminal J5 is tied across the 3.3 V heater-control net to GND. Power-mux, buck, heater high-side switch, USB and TVS items otherwise match the documented (non-anomaly) reference.
